purpose: End-to-end pipeline validation and instrument calibration on 8 items (2 per class, overlapping the frozen 80) BEFORE the confirmatory run; not a result
command: python experiments/run_lexical_closeness.py --config smoke8.json --systems Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --out pipeline_smoke_8; python experiments/analyze_lexical_closeness.py --run pipeline_smoke_8
notes: Preregistered robustness rule (|median|>3*MAD over 4 paraphrases) is unreachable: paraphrases within a block differ in KL scale by up to 16x, so paraphrase MAD measures carrier scale heterogeneity, not noise. Closeness orderings reproduce across paraphrases far above chance; directed asymmetry signs do not (approx chance). Design must be amended before the 80-item run: per-paraphrase scale normalization, sign rule with a proper chance null, and a stronger asymmetry measurement. Disclosed in the preregistration amendment.
Highest-leverage item is the instrument's robustness rule and the asymmetry measurement, being settled with Codex before the confirmatory run. No plumbing drift.

purpose: NLM-002 non-LM branch (CIFAR-100/DINOv2), locked pre-scoring with two recorded implementation decisions
notes: M2 kill condition met: raw-pixel k=32 kNN fine-label endpoint is nearly uninformative (0.115 accuracy; 0.12 agreement with embedding kNN), so the locked endpoint is invalid and M3 (F vs R tie, delta -0.004 [-0.034,0.026]) is a tie on noise, not a primitive verdict. M1 informative: coarse-semantic readout monotone along chart-straight embedding lines in ~98% of same-class paths; pixel-stat heads flicker 21-24% (heads are weak, 52-59% test acc); any-readout 51%. Prereg predicted >=60% any-readout flicker: not met for same-class. Lesson: an endpoint must be independent AND informative; the true fine label (no head trained on it) is both.

purpose: NLM-003 (locked e2a1fb2): F vs R with the true fine-label consequence endpoint on the frozen CIFAR-100/DINOv2 artifact
notes: Preregistered gate met: R beats F by >=5pp (CI upper bound -0.058 < -0.05). Decisive context: both native constructs lose by 20-30pp to plain cosine/Euclidean in the DINOv2 chart on the informative endpoint. Support thin: 270/400 anchors had no same-fine-class candidate among 40 draws (100 classes). Interpretation for the guiding question: a world whose encoder is trained to make one chart metric meaningful makes that metric the denizen's best map; the native constructs as built are worse maps than the imported one here.
Highest-leverage: adjudicating why the chart metric dominates in every world tested and finding a world/move where it cannot (composition, null world). Not plumbing.
